newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH KOMERCNI CHIEF CALLS FOR QUICK PRIVATISATION.
newsitem.headline: CZECH KOMERCNI CHIEF CALLS FOR QUICK PRIVATISATION.

text.p: The privatisation of Komercni Banka a.s. , the largest Czech commercial bank, should occur as quickly as possible and include foreign participants, the bank's director said on Tuesday.

Speaking at the FIBEX banking and finance exhibition, Komercni General Director Richard Salzmann said the state should sell its entire 48.7 percent stake in the bank, to allow it increased access to capital.

"I belive Komercni should be privatised as quickly and openly as possible," he said. "And I don't think it can be done only through Czech capital since there is not enough available, it must include foreigners as well."

Salzmann said that the matter was purely up to the government to decide, but that he hoped the government's recent announcement that privatisation, including banks, must move forward quickly would mean a sell-off sooner, rather than later.
Last week the government said that as part of its economic stimulus programme, it was charging the Finance Ministry to come up with a proposal for privatising the banks by the end of May.
The state also holds large stakes in three other banks -- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s., Ceska Sporitelna a.s. and IPB a.s. .
It is currently setting conditions for a tender to sell its 36 percent stake in IPB.

Earlier on Tuesday, the Slovak National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, said it was preparing to open negotiations with an unspecified Asian financial investor over the sale of its 15 percent stake in Komercni.
Slovakia was given the stake when the former Czechoslovakia split in 1993.
